correctness.rationale: For fixed finite vocabulary and rational nondegenerate type/edge masses, the root row is exactly multinomial with an independent root type and self-loop. An inductive case split eliminates all current-state indicator terms into finite affine tests on the counts. Since all selected types and the nonedge outcome have positive masses, the multinomial covariance is strictly positive definite: u^T Sigma u >= lambda(1-lambda) E_nu(u_s^2). LLN resolves nonzero-drift comparisons and joint multivariate CLT with null hyperplane boundaries resolves balanced nonzero comparisons. Finite sign-cell decomposition produces a Gaussian-cone formula. Positive Gaussian density and rescaling strict homogeneous inequalities to >=1 give an effective rational LP test for 0/1 endpoints. The bivariate witness has exact mean 0, variance 1/2 and 3/2, covariance 1/2, and irrational arcsine constant by root-of-unity algebraic integrality. The packaged checker exhaustively corroborates the exact finite multinomial census through five worlds and full graphs through three; finite tests are not asserted to prove asymptotics.

value.rationale: Qualitative verification of a one-step count-aggregation modal query on a large random labelled graph requires determining whether the satisfaction frequency asymptotically vanishes, tends to one, or remains nontrivial, even when count comparisons have exactly zero mean. The theorem gives a terminating exact rational LP procedure for both endpoints across a complete natural depth-one fragment with full root-indicator nesting, a closed finite multinomial census and Gaussian-cone representation, and a motivated irrational limit showing genuinely intermediate behavior. It solves a concrete restricted form of the graph-probability decision direction identified in a 2026 primary paper. No larger-depth or complexity-uniformity claims are made.
